sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression assessed in heterologous cells (the purpose of the tagged construct); odorant-evoked functional assay not described in the cited clip.
sites.rationale: OR4A16 is a 7-TM olfactory receptor with no signal peptide; the topology landmarks place residues 1–24 extracellular and residues 288–328 intracellular, leaving the N-terminus as the sole extracellular terminus. L1 explicitly reports N-terminal FLAG and rhodopsin epitope tags on the full-length receptor, so the tag prepends before M1 (insert_after_residue = 0). No residue number is named in the clip, so the position is topology-derived rather than validated. Python confirmed residue 1 = M, consistent with residue_after = 'M'. Full-length OR4A16 cloned into pME18S with N-terminal FLAG epitope tag and 20 N-terminal amino acids of bovine rhodopsin fused upstream of the receptor, expressed heterologously. The construct is full-length and membrane-anchored.

sources.claim: Each of the amplified receptor genes was inserted into the pME18S vector to generate OR proteins fused with N-terminal epitope tags of FLAG and 20 N-terminal amino acids of bovine rhodopsin.

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) is provided. It supports a single N-terminal prepend site derived from topology (the N-terminus is the only extracellular terminus of this 7-TM receptor). No residue number is named in the clip, so position_evidence is topology_derived and cited_tag_residue is null. No internal loop insertions are grounded by the ledger. The C-terminus (288–328) is intracellular and therefore not a surface-tag site. ECL1 (78–95), ECL2 (163–191), and ECL3 (258–267) are extracellular but no ledger line grounds any insertion in them.
